ops.title: fusekit v0.37.0 (Track C) ships holder-hosted FP content bridge — content.RelaySource + mountd OpAddBridge/OpRemoveBridge/OpBridges — but the cc-pool cutover (moving b.sock into the holder) is deferred to Track D; the fusekit capability shipped AHEAD o
ops.body:
**Shipped 2026-07-09 as fusekit v0.37.0** (tag da82d131, cask `fusekit-holder v0.37.0`). Track C = a step toward [[fusekit-global-holder-direction]]: the shared holder can now host a consumer daemon's File-Provider-facing content bridge, so the FP appex keeps enumerating/saving across daemon restarts.

- **fusekit side is DONE and released; cc-pool side is DEFERRED to Track D** (user decision). The holder becomes a stable-path *container* client (owns the FP-facing `b.sock` bind) only in Track D, before it owns FP consent. So the capability exists in fusekit but nothing consumes it yet — cc-pool's go.mod still needs the pin bump when Track D lands. Don't assume cc-pool's daemon-side FP bridge moved; it did not.
- **What v0.37.0 added.** `content.RelaySource` (in `content/relay.go`): a caching, write-spooling `content.Source` proxying the consumer daemon's bridge over `content.BridgeClient`. Additive proto-1 mountd ops `OpAddBridge`/`OpRemoveBridge`/`OpBridges` + `Request.BridgeSocket` (appex-facing socket the holder BINDS) + `Response.Bridges []BridgeInfo`. Bridge registry is SEPARATE from the mount registry (no sweep/converge/carcass ever sees it).
- **Design premise CORRECTED during build:** the Swift FP appex sends **no `domain` on classify** (`widget/Sources/FileProvider/BridgeClient.swift` sends domain only for manifest/read/write). So `content.Classifier.ClassifyErr(name)` is domain-LESS; offline classify consults the union of cached manifests (cc-pool classification is domain-agnostic anyway).
- **Security invariants baked in (a codex+lead review caught 9 defects; all fixed in the released tag — do NOT regress):** (1) offline `classifyOffline` is FAIL-CLOSED — unknown name → `ErrClassifyUnavailable`, never shared, because cc-pool's glob/case private patterns (`*.lock`, `.Credentials.json`) are not on the wire; (2) the write spool is seq-qualified (`<key>.<seq>`) so a replay never unlinks a newer acked write, bounded (1024 entries / 64 MiB, `ErrSpoolFull`), and rejects NUL/empty targets; (3) wire `Owner` MUST be a safe single path segment (`ClassInvalidOwner`) — it names `~/.fusekit/spool/<owner>`, and `x/../victim` would else cross-tenant-exfil another owner's spool; (4) at most ONE live `RelaySource` per spool dir ever (reclaim keeps a `stopping` row so a same-owner re-add refuses `ClassBusy`).
